title: Confession and Ledger
premise: Sebastian Pemberton, the observant concierge of the Grand Meridian Hotel, is hired by a nervous widow who insists her husband will be murdered next week and wants it proven before it happens. Following the money trail through a shipping ledger disguised as a guest register, Sebastian uncovers an inheritance scheme entwined with his own hidden past as the disinherited son of the family being targeted. In the climax at the tidal causeway, he exposes the killer — the widow herself, whose 'pre-payment' was a confession seeking a witness to absolve her — and chooses to claim his true name rather than remain invisible.
about_author: Tamsin Brightwater spent a decade working night desks in coastal hotels, collecting the stories guests tell strangers at 3 a.m. She writes mysteries about people who see everything and are seen by no one.

chapters.title: The Advance Payment
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. A wealthy widow, Mrs. Ashcombe, pays Sebastian handsomely to prove her husband's murder has not yet occurred, leaving only a torn ledger page as evidence. Sebastian's instinct for patterns tells him the request itself is the crime scene. Emotional beat: unease — the watcher realizes he is being watched back.

chapters.title: Entries in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Decoding the ledger hidden in the hotel's guest register, Sebastian finds dates matching three past 'accidents' and discovers the Ashcombe inheritance flows through his own estranged family name. Emotional beat: vertigo — his invisibility was a choice that protected a lie about who he is.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV alternating Sebastian and Mrs. Ashcombe. As the predicted murder date arrives, Sebastian races to the causeway where the ledger's final entry points; the tide reveals a body that isn't the husband's but the first victim's, finally surfaced. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve as the two POVs converge on the same shore.

chapters.title: Confession and Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Confronting Mrs. Ashcombe, Sebastian learns she orchestrated everything: the payment was her confession, the murder a trap to force someone competent to witness her guilt and stop her from becoming what she feared. He names her to the police — and signs his own real name for the first time in years. Emotional beat: release; identity claimed, duty and love reconciled.
